sections.title: Global Workplace Dynamics
sections.description:
Organizational studies students and practitioners must be aware of global forces, organizational actors, and employee behaviors that converge to create the visible and invisible dynamics that shape the goals, objectives and experiences of organizational life. Additionally, students and practitioners must be able to hold a cognitive frame that can notice and synthesize changing global contexts, adjust to shifting organizational strategies, and tend to evolving employee needs and demands.
This course will expose the student to the interdependencies that influence societal priorities, global organization strategy, leadership behavior, and employee experience. This course explores global workforce dynamics through a multi-level systems lens—macro (global governance, globalization, socio-political forces, and global demographics), meso (organizational structures, environmental scanning, and global leadership), and micro (individual experience and behavior in organizations). Students analyze how globalization, national culture, global governance, demographics, and labor trends shape organizational realities and influence and are influenced by interactions of global, organizational, and employee systems. Through the use of various multi-analytic frameworks, students will interrogate how organizations operate, adapt, and lead in increasingly complex environments.
This learning environment and coursework will challenge students’ conceptual and mental models of norms and global truths by exposing them to diverse perspectives and alternative frames. An overarching goal of the course is to challenge students’ worldviews, as well as their organization and cultural assumptions, while moving them toward relevant solutions and applications for use in their day-to-day roles as organizational actors.
This course and instruction will engage students through class discussion, experiential exercises, case study reviews, individual and group projects, and written assignments. Students will integrate theory with practice, applying systems thinking to examine how macro forces translate into organizational decision-making and individual experiences in multinational environments.
